Action Plan:
1. Increase Furosemide from “1 tablet once daily” to “1 tablet twice daily” for the next few days; continue Aspirin and Bisoprolol unchanged.
2. Arrange same-day phlebotomy for CBC, U&E/creatinine, and electrolytes.
3. Request outpatient transthoracic echocardiogram within 1–2 weeks to reassess left-ventricular function.
4. Review in 1 week (earlier if worsening breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness).
5. Safety-net: advise patient to seek urgent care if symptoms acutely deteriorate.
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 66-year-old male (name: Oscar) presents with progressive shortness of breath for 2 weeks, markedly worse over the last few days; now breathless walking short distances and at home.  
• Associated symptoms: mild dry cough, bilateral ankle swelling (past 3 days), feels “run-down.”  
• Denies chest pain, palpitations, fever, orthostatic symptoms. Appetite and urinary output unchanged (polyuria attributed to diuretics).  
• Past medical history: chronic heart failure; “small heart attack” ≈5 years ago (probable MI). No other chronic conditions reported.  
• Medications:  
  – Furosemide (dose not documented; 1 tablet daily)  
  – Aspirin (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
  – Bisoprolol (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
• Allergies: none known.  
• Family history: father died of myocardial infarction (early 60s); mother alive with osteoporosis.  
• Social: lives alone with two cats; part-time lorry driver; ex-smoker (≈1 pack/day × 25 yrs, quit); denies alcohol; limited exercise (walks to shops).

Objective:
• Vitals: values not provided; clinician stated oxygen saturation and blood pressure “OK.”  
• Chest examination reportedly normal (details not documented).  
• Peripheral: bilateral ankle oedema (extent not quantified).  
• No additional physical findings documented.  
• Investigations to date: none yet performed.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Worsening shortness of breath / possible acute decompensated heart failure  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute decompensated (congestive) heart failure (DDx rank: High).  
   – Differential diagnosis:  
     • Lower-respiratory tract infection precipitating HF (Medium likelihood) – mild dry cough, systemic malaise but afebrile and clear chest exam.  
     • Pulmonary embolism (Low–Medium) – sedentary occupation; less likely due to gradual onset and bilateral rather than unilateral leg findings.  
     • Anemia (Low) – will be assessed on CBC.  
   – Investigations planned: CBC, renal panel/electrolytes, transthoracic echocardiogram.  
   – Treatment planned: Increase Furosemide to 1 tablet twice daily; continue current Aspirin and Bisoprolol; monitor symptoms; provide escalation advice.  
   – Relevant referrals: Echocardiogram booking (cardiology diagnostics).

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: exact patient age, vital-sign values, orthopnea/PND history, current Furosemide dose in mg, weights, fluid intake guidance, vaccination status, full medication reconciliation.  
● Internal conflicts: none noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: generally clear; occasional connectivity drop (minor inaudible words) but clinical content preserved.
